meta.verdict_states_note: Condition states (met / with a change / not met / not applicable or declined / cannot judge / not judged) describe single conditions only. There is no match verdict: decided 13 Oct 2026 — the tool lays out trade-offs by party and does not rank or score options. Wording is suggested for J.B. to accept.
meta.source_roles_note: source_roles (added 12 Oct 2026): for each source, the term of the formula it supplies, its role (coefficient · bound · proxy · check · site fact · rule · data · method · gap) and its own confidence on the register scale; verified=false marks a placement that is Claude's reading of the coefficient text rather than an explicit tie, for J.B. to confirm. A quantity's own confidence is not recomputed from these: it was set in verification and can sit below its sources where the transfer or an assumption is the weak link (status says why), or above a source used only as a check or bound. The md lists every quantity where own confidence differs from the lowest coefficient-role source, for review.

quantities.name: Heat-pump COP (Lorenz)
quantities.formula: COP = η × T_lm,sink ÷ (T_lm,sink − T_lm,source), log-mean temperatures on both sides (sink supply/return; source in/out); η 0.40–0.50 for built systems (calibrated 13 Oct 2026), 0.50–0.60 upper bound

The simplified form used in the first attempt (sink supply ÷ (sink supply − source out)) under-predicts at large lifts (3.0–3.6 for Odense) and is retired
quantities.status: calibrated on six cases: η 0.39–0.53 built/operating

quantities.name: Heat captured at the boundary (E_reuse)
quantities.formula: E_reuse = heat_rejected × liquid_capture, measured at the data-centre boundary by flow × ΔT before any heat pump (ISO/IEC 30134-6 cl.5–6; EU Reg. 2024/1364 Annex II 1(j))
quantities.coef: This is the figure a data centre may report as reused energy and the numerator of ERF; the network-side figure after the heat pump (what Stockholm Exergi and Fjernvarme Fyn meter and bill, and what Danish tax law meters "ved udgang fra varmepumpe" with 3 × electricity deducted) is heat_delivered, not E_reuse. quantities.name: Water licence required
quantities.formula: BC: yes for open-loop heat exchange (WSR Sch. A item 9). Alberta (Guide to Groundwater Authorization 2023 §6.2): open loop with no water loss and return to the same water body = Water Act "activity" → approval; different water body or any loss → licence; closed loop → none. Flow tier for the aquifer test: Q(m³/day) = heat_kW ÷ (1.16 × ΔT) × 24; a 1 MW loop at ΔT 5 K ≈ 4,100 m³/day → top tier
quantities.coef: Alberta EPA fact sheet, Ground Source Heat Exchange Systems (8 Oct 2025; 2024 edition identical on these points): open-loop systems "are regulated through a Water Act authorization" obtained before construction; application must assess the aquifer's capability to circulate the required quantity continuously, effects on groundwater quantity, temperature and quality, and on household, agricultural and existing licence holders; complex systems need an APEGA groundwater specialist report per the Guide to Groundwater Authorization; water in an open loop cannot be used for another purpose or temporarily discharged; open-loop wells drilled by a Class A driller, return through a separate return well; horizontal closed loop above the water table and vertical closed loop above the base of groundwater protection need no Water Act authorization (Class F installer); below the base of groundwater protection the AER regulates under the Geothermal Resource Development Act; applications via DRAS. Directive (11 Dec 2018) sets the construction standards; Guide App. 2 aquifer-test tiers by daily pumping rate: ≤10 m³/day 2+2 h, no observation well, no APEGA report (§2.2); 10–35 m³/day 24+24 h, 0–1 obs well; 35–65 m³/day 24+24 h, 1; 65–265 m³/day 48+48 h, 1–2; >265 m³/day 72+72 h, 1–2 obs wells, full §2 report by an APEGA groundwater practitioner; maximum daily rate = lesser of test rate and Q20 (20-year sustainable yield); CSA C448 referenced for installation; temporary discharge needs the director's authorisation
quantities.status: BC and Alberta both confirmed from the regulator (data/); Alberta open loop = Water Act authorization with a temperature-impact assessment — a pass/partial condition, not a veto
